# Requirements

Every byte of user content Matrix persists today is plaintext: conversations and archives (neo/internal/conversation, JSONL), Neo traces and workspace timelines (neo/internal/trace, JSONL), executor transcripts and Construct surfaces (JSONL), tasks / async jobs / conversation metadata / intent envelopes / Automatrix settings (JSON), the entire cortex (memories, sessions, journal, rollups, vectors as plaintext values in Pebble), media, screenshots, snapshots, and backups — written 0644 into 0755 directories. Half A of this feature builds ONE shared encrypted-storage layer (a new top-level vault module) used by Neo, Cortex, the executor daemon, and Construct: envelope encryption (platform KEK behind a KMS seam, a separately wrapped per-user key, per-object DEKs), AES-256-GCM AEAD per NIST SP 800-38D via Go crypto/cipher, key ids + format versions stored with ciphertext and never raw keys, per-record JSONL encryption so append/recovery/trimming/streaming keep working, whole-file AEAD for atomic JSON, chunked streaming AEAD for media and snapshots, and cortex encryption BELOW its logical encoding + hashing boundary so MMR/SMT/journal roots stay deterministic over logical data while randomized ciphertext is persisted. Production fails closed — no KMS, no plaintext fallback. Deletion becomes a pipeline: disable collection, cancel alarms and jobs, destroy the wrapped user key (cryptographic erasure over all backups), delete ciphertext from active storage / snapshots / training staging on a documented retention schedule, and produce a deletion receipt; training consent stays a separate grant with full export lineage. Half B builds personalization ON that substrate: explicit opt-in (default off), a short guided interview (five skippable question groups, one at a time, confirmed as a plain-language summary before saving), ONE versioned tagged cortex personalization record (never overloading expertise_domains, never fragmented inferred memories), separate schedule state, a dedicated MORNING_BRIEF Chronos alarm in the user's timezone, and a restricted supervised brief run (read-only information tools only) that composes a source-backed, non-repeating morning brief delivered as a normal conversation turn. The main new work is the vault, the personalization schema + interview, the brief scheduling/policy/history, and client surfaces — not a new autonomy framework: the Automatrix settings/governor/wake/restricted-surface/supervisor patterns are reused wholesale.

## Requirement 1: The vault: one shared envelope-encryption layer

**User Story:** As the platform owner, I want a single encrypted-storage library used by Neo, Cortex, Executor, and Construct, so that user data at rest is protected uniformly rather than by ad-hoc per-store patches.

### Acceptance Criteria

1. A new top-level module vault/ SHALL implement envelope encryption: a platform key-encryption key behind a KeyProvider seam (file/env provider for dev, remote KMS provider shape for prod), a separately wrapped per-user key minted at provision and stored only in wrapped form, and a fresh random data-encryption key per file/object wrapped by the user key.
2. ALL encryption SHALL be authenticated (AES-256-GCM via Go crypto/cipher, per NIST SP 800-38D) with random 96-bit nonces and one DEK per object; decryption failures SHALL be indistinguishable between disclosure and tampering (a single authentication error).
3. EVERY ciphertext object SHALL carry a versioned self-describing header (magic, format version, key id, wrapped DEK, AD schema version); raw key bytes SHALL never be persisted, logged, or returned in errors.
4. WHEN VAULT_REQUIRED is true (production default) and the KeyProvider or user key is unavailable, THE vault SHALL fail writes with a hard error and the daemon SHALL refuse to boot into plaintext mode; no code path SHALL fall back to plaintext writes.
5. KEK rotation SHALL re-wrap user keys without rewriting data objects, and user-key rotation SHALL be expressible per user; keys SHALL never be reused between users.

## Requirement 2: Record-encrypted JSONL stores

**User Story:** As a user, I want every conversation turn, trace event, transcript line, and surface frame encrypted independently, so that my history is sealed while append, recovery, retention trimming, and streaming reads keep working.

### Acceptance Criteria

1. THE vault SHALL provide an encrypted JSONL reader/writer where each record is an independent AEAD ciphertext line, preserving O(1) O_APPEND appends, skip-torn-tail crash recovery, retention trimming/archive rollup, and line-streamed reads.
2. EACH record's associated data SHALL bind the user DID, store type, conversation/run id, record sequence, and schema version, such that a record moved between users, stores, conversations, or positions fails authentication.
3. THE Neo conversation store (hot + archive + meta), the Neo trace store, the Construct surface store, and the executor daemon's transcripts and conversation threads SHALL write through the encrypted JSONL layer.
4. READS SHALL sniff the header: encrypted records decrypt, legacy plaintext lines parse as today (until migration completes), and new writes SHALL always be encrypted once the vault is wired.

## Requirement 3: Whole-file encryption for atomic JSON

**User Story:** As a user, I want my task records, queued jobs, settings, and intent envelopes sealed, so that operational metadata about me is as protected as my conversations.

### Acceptance Criteria

1. THE vault SHALL provide whole-file AEAD for tmp+rename atomic JSON files, with associated data binding user DID, store type, and file role.
2. THE Neo task ledger, executor async-job registry, conversation meta sidecars, Automatrix settings/inbox stores, and persisted intent envelopes SHALL write through it, preserving tmp+rename atomicity.

## Requirement 4: Cortex encryption below the hash boundary

**User Story:** As a user, I want my memories, sessions, journal, and embeddings encrypted inside Pebble, so that the most intimate store is sealed without breaking cortex's deterministic integrity anchoring.

### Acceptance Criteria

1. CORTEX SHALL encrypt Pebble VALUES (journal entries, memory heads/versions, session records, rollups, story-so-far, checkpoints, embedding vectors) at the store write seam, decrypting before decode on every read.
2. JOURNAL leaf hashes, SMT value hashes, and OverallRoot SHALL remain computed over the canonical plaintext logical encodings, byte-identical before and after encryption; a test SHALL prove OverallRoot equality across a plaintext-to-encrypted migration and across replay.
3. RESIDUAL leakage (Pebble key prefixes, ids, sizes, access patterns) SHALL be documented, with volume/database encryption stated as a required complementary layer.

## Requirement 5: Media, snapshots, backups: streaming encryption

**User Story:** As a user, I want my screenshots, generated files, uploads, and full-machine snapshots encrypted, so that backups and the object store never hold my content in the clear.

### Acceptance Criteria

1. THE vault SHALL provide chunked streaming AEAD (framed chunks, per-chunk AD with index + final flag) so truncation and reordering fail closed; media files and large exports SHALL write through it.
2. DAEMON snapshot tarballs SHALL be vault-encrypted before push to the S3/MinIO bucket, and restore SHALL decrypt-verify; a restore round-trip test SHALL run on real files.

## Requirement 6: Permission tightening and the plaintext production gate

**User Story:** As the platform owner, I want the filesystem hardened immediately and a gate that catches any plaintext regression, so that protection does not silently erode.

### Acceptance Criteria

1. SENSITIVE data directories SHALL be created 0700 and files 0600 across the conversation, trace, surface, task, async, settings, media, snapshot, and cortex stores; tests SHALL assert modes on really-created paths.
2. A plaintext scanner SHALL walk a user's data tree and fail on forbidden plaintext content artifacts (parseable JSON/JSONL content without a vault header) for migrated users, wired as a production/CI gate.

## Requirement 7: Migration: versioned, quiesced, never dual-write

**User Story:** As an operator, I want existing users migrated to encrypted storage safely, so that no data is lost and no window dual-writes plaintext.

### Acceptance Criteria

1. VERSIONED readers SHALL make all new writes encrypted immediately while legacy plaintext remains readable until migrated.
2. THE migrator SHALL quiesce one user at a time, encrypt each file into a temporary sibling, verify record counts and full authenticated round trips, then atomically replace the plaintext original; plaintext SHALL never be dual-written during migration.
3. CORTEX migration SHALL rewrite values in batches and prove OverallRoot byte-identity before/after.

## Requirement 8: Deletion: pipeline, cryptographic erasure, receipt

**User Story:** As a user, I want deletion to be immediate in effect and provable in outcome, so that leaving the platform genuinely removes me.

### Acceptance Criteria

1. DELETION SHALL immediately disable personalization and training collection and cancel the user's Chronos alarms and background jobs.
2. DELETION SHALL destroy the user's wrapped encryption key, rendering all remaining ciphertext (including every backup/snapshot generation) unreadable from that instant.
3. DELETION SHALL delete ciphertext from active storage, MinIO snapshot generations (including old object versions), and training staging per a documented retention schedule.
4. DELETION SHALL produce a durable receipt/status (per-stage outcome, timestamps) and preserve only minimal non-content compliance records where legally required.

## Requirement 9: Training-consent lineage, separate from personalization

**User Story:** As a user, I want training use of my data to be its own consent with full lineage, so that revoking it stops exports and deletes what was staged.

### Acceptance Criteria

1. TRAINING consent (router Postgres) SHALL remain independent of the personalization opt-in; neither grant implies the other.
2. EVERY training export SHALL carry a manifest: consent version, consent time, source record IDs, user/pseudonymous identity, and export batch id.
3. REVOCATION SHALL stop future exports at selection and initiate deletion through the recorded dataset lineage; training datasets SHALL use their own vault keys and access roles, disjoint from user-data keys.

## Requirement 10: Adversarial no-fakes verification of the vault

**User Story:** As the owner, I want the encryption layer proven against real attacks on real storage paths, so that protection is demonstrated, not asserted.

### Acceptance Criteria

1. TESTS on real storage paths SHALL prove: wrong-user key fails decryption; flipped ciphertext bytes and cross-context record swaps fail authentication; truncated records/chunks are detected or safely skipped per shape; a crash mid-append leaves a readable store.
2. TESTS SHALL prove KEK rotation re-wraps without data rewrite, snapshot backup/restore round-trips, and post-deletion unreadability of prior ciphertext.
3. NO test in this feature SHALL substitute a fake for a real code path: real vault, real files, real Pebble, real engine.

## Requirement 11: Personalization opt-in and settings surface

**User Story:** As a user, I want personalization off by default with full control in Settings, so that Neo only knows what I chose to share and briefs arrive only how I want them.

### Acceptance Criteria

1. PERSONALIZATION and the morning brief SHALL be OFF by default; enabling is an explicit user action.
2. SETTINGS SHALL let the user: enable/disable the morning brief, start/repeat/edit the interview, select delivery time, IANA timezone, days, and brief length, choose sections (news, music, movies/TV, books, games, daily assistance), view and delete the saved profile, and pause briefs without deleting preferences.
3. DISABLING SHALL cancel future briefs immediately (alarm cancelled, zero scheduled network retrieval) while retaining the profile unless the user separately deletes it.

## Requirement 12: Guided interview with confirmation

**User Story:** As a user, I want a short guided conversation that asks about me one topic at a time and shows me what it understood, so that only what I confirm is saved.

### Acceptance Criteria

1. WHEN enabled, Neo SHALL run a guided interview of roughly five question groups, one at a time: interests/topics; day-to-day help; media tastes liked and disliked (music, films, shows, books, games, creators); recommendation adventurousness (familiar|balanced|surprising); brief delivery time/timezone/detail.
2. EVERY question SHALL be skippable; skipped groups leave their schema fields empty.
3. NEO SHALL present a plain-language profile summary for confirmation BEFORE saving; nothing is persisted to the profile without confirmation, and interview conversations SHALL be excluded from writeback fact/opportunity extraction so answers never become fragmented inferred memories.

## Requirement 13: The personalization profile record

**User Story:** As a user, I want my confirmed profile stored as one inspectable, versioned record, so that I can see, edit, export, and delete exactly what Neo knows about me.

### Acceptance Criteria

1. THE confirmed profile SHALL be ONE versioned, tagged, pinned cortex record with a dedicated schema (interests, day-to-day goals, media tastes with dislikes, adventurousness, brief preferences) — NOT an overload of the onboarding profile's expertise_domains.
2. THE daemon SHALL expose authenticated view/edit/export/delete endpoints for the record, mirroring the /profile route posture; deletion SHALL remove the record and its history from the authoritative surface.
3. THE schema SHALL contain no inferred sensitive-trait fields, and profile mutations SHALL only originate from confirmed interview output, explicit Settings edits, or explicit recommendation feedback.

## Requirement 14: Brief schedule state and the MORNING_BRIEF alarm

**User Story:** As a user, I want my brief to arrive at my chosen local time on my chosen days, so that scheduling is correct across timezones and DST.

### Acceptance Criteria

1. SCHEDULE state SHALL live in a dedicated durable settings sidecar, separate from the profile: enabled, timezone, local delivery time, selected days, brief length, sections, paused, alarm id, destination conversation, last-delivered date.
2. A dedicated MORNING_BRIEF Chronos convention (sibling of AUTOMATRIX) SHALL define the wake marker and alarm shape; enabling SHALL create exactly ONE recurring alarm at the user's local time in their IANA timezone (idempotency-keyed), settings changes SHALL reschedule it, and disable/pause SHALL cancel or skip it — DST correctness comes from Chronos cron+timezone scheduling.
3. THE wake handler SHALL re-read settings on EVERY fire (fail closed on a nil governor), skip non-selected days and already-delivered dates, and never deliver twice for one local date.

## Requirement 15: The restricted, supervised brief run

**User Story:** As a user, I want the autonomous brief run structurally unable to touch money or my machine, and durable against restarts, so that a scheduled agent run is safe and reliable.

### Acceptance Criteria

1. THE brief run SHALL execute on a positive tool allowlist tighter than Automatrix — recent-news search, web search, fetch/read-only information tools, and memory recall only; financial, signing, filesystem, deployment, and arbitrary-execution tools (including core_execute) SHALL be structurally absent from the advertised schema set, proven against the REAL advertised surface.
2. THE run SHALL be supervised through the durable task ledger so a dropped connection or daemon restart resumes an in-progress brief; the finished brief SHALL be durably persisted (conversation turn + inbox record) before any live notification.
3. WHEN personalization or the brief is disabled at wake time, THE handler SHALL perform zero network retrieval.

## Requirement 16: Brief content policy

**User Story:** As a user, I want a short, source-backed, honest brief, so that news is current and recommendations are explained rather than spammed.

### Acceptance Criteria

1. A brief SHALL contain at most five news items across the user's interests; every news claim SHALL derive from fresh web retrieval in the run (never model memory) and carry a publication date and source link, plus a short why-relevant explanation.
2. A brief SHALL include one or two rotating recommendations (not every category daily) and a small 'Neo can help today' section derived from the stated day-to-day goals.
3. THE brief SHALL distinguish current facts from recommendations, and SHALL contain no sponsored or affiliate recommendations without clear disclosure.

## Requirement 17: Recommendation history and explicit feedback

**User Story:** As a user, I want Neo to remember what it already recommended and learn from my explicit reactions, so that briefs stay fresh and steadily better fit me.

### Acceptance Criteria

1. DELIVERED recommendation identifiers and news source URLs SHALL be recorded in a durable history sidecar consulted at composition; a recommendation SHALL NOT repeat unless genuinely new context exists.
2. EXPLICIT feedback ('liked', 'not interested', 'show me less of this') SHALL update the history and flow into the profile only as explicit user-attributed preference entries — never as silent inference.

## Requirement 18: Half-B verification on the real engine

**User Story:** As the owner, I want the personalization loop proven end-to-end on real components, so that opt-in gating, scheduling, restriction, and durability are demonstrated.

### Acceptance Criteria

1. PROPERTY tests on the real engine SHALL prove: default-off + opt-in gating (a wake with the feature off performs zero tool dispatches), alarm lifecycle idempotence (exactly one alarm across repeated enables), day/date delivery guards, and the structural tool exclusion via the real advertised schema set.
2. AN end-to-end test SHALL drive interview -> confirmation -> profile record -> wake -> supervised run (real httptest-backed search/fetch tools) -> durable brief + history, including supervisor resume of an interrupted brief and the no-repeat property.
